content:
The new Apple TV 4K was long overdue, originally expected to launch last fall. However, with Siri AI finally ready to go, all signs point to the new Apple TV 4K making its debut—very possibly at the September 9 event. Here are the latest rumours.

First: Siri Remote Update

No specific details have leaked yet, but Apple is reportedly set to release an updated version of the Siri Remote alongside the new Apple TV 4K.

Code from a beta version of macOS 26.7 appears to confirm the existence of a new Siri Remote. And before this leak, Mark Gurman had already reported that the new hardware may come with an "improved Apple TV remote".

It doesn't look like there will be major changes, but here's hoping for at least an upgrade to the second-generation ultra-wideband chip to support Precision Finding.

Second: Siri AI and More Apple Intelligence Features

Siri AI is expected to be the key marketing focus of the new Apple TV and other new home products.

Apple has yet to reveal whether the new assistant will come to the Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But growing evidence suggests that tvOS 27 will feature built-in Siri AI, and it may only support the new hardware.

There's a good chance other Apple Intelligence features will also be added, such as an enhanced search experience.

Third: All-New A-Series Chip

The current Apple TV uses the A15 Bionic chip that first debuted in 2021. The good news is that the new model will see a significant performance boost.

It will come equipped with a more powerful, brand-new A-series chip capable of supporting AI features.

Rumours suggest it could be the A17 Pro or A18 chip, but most of these reports predate the launch of Siri AI. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple instead opts for an even more powerful A19 or A20 chip.

Fourth: N1 Wireless Chip

The N1 wireless chip that first appeared in the iPhone 17 is also rumoured to make its way into the new Apple TV 4K.

With the N1 onboard, the Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as Thread networking.

By comparison, the current Apple TV hardware, now four years old, only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features do you hope to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
